title: Ham & Cheddar Breakfast Strata
subtitle: a make-ahead bread, ham and cheddar bake that puffs up golden in the morning
imageAlt: A golden puffed ham and cheddar breakfast strata in a baking dish with one square served on a cream plate beside a navy napkin
servingsNote: a 9×13 dish: brunch for two, plus 4 portions for the week

beforeYouStart.text: Assemble it the night before: it needs at least 2 hours in the fridge so the bread soaks up the custard.
Take it out of the fridge while the oven heats.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Butter a 23×33 cm (9×13 in) baking dish. Scatter half the bread, then half the ham and cheddar; repeat.

steps.title: Custard
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, milk, onion powder, salt and pepper and pour it evenly over the dish. Press the bread down so it soaks.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours, or overnight.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F). Bake uncovered 45–55 minutes, until puffed, golden and 74°C (165°F) in the centre and a knife comes out clean.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Rest 10 minutes, then cut into squares.

fixIt.fix: Bake longer until it reads 74°C (165°F); tent with foil if the top browns first.
Use day-old bread, not toasted, and soak it at least 2 hours.
Lay foil loosely over it for the last 15 minutes.

saleTip: Ask the No Frills deli counter for ham ends; they're cheaper and perfect chopped.
swap: Cooked crumbled sausage or bacon for ham. Swiss for cheddar.
leftovers: Squares reheat well for weekday breakfasts or lunch.
doneness: Egg dishes to 74°C (165°F) in the centre (Health Canada); the ham is fully cooked.
source: Based on tested make-ahead strata methods (Canadian Living, America's Test Kitchen): cubed day-old bread soaked overnight in an egg and milk custard, baked at 175°C until set.
prepAhead: Assemble up to 24 hours ahead and keep covered in the fridge.
reheat: Squares covered in the microwave 1–2 minutes, or at 180°C (350°F) for 15 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Ham, cheddar, eggs and milk; no onion powder.

fancy.note: Gruyère and soft sautéed onion through the layers.

addSteps.title: Onion first
addSteps.text: Before layering, cook the onion in the butter over medium-low 10 minutes until soft and golden. Layer it and the Gruyère with the ham.

plating: Cut neat squares with a hot knife.

why.0-1: Day-old bread soaks up custard without turning to mush.
why.1-0: Eight eggs to two cups of milk sets into a tender, sliceable custard.

funFact: 'Strata' is Latin for layers; the dish became a North American church-brunch favourite in the mid-1900s.
drink: Coffee and orange juice, or a pot of English Breakfast tea.
